extraction.note: Imported so that the results which renormalise without a regulator, by extension of distributions across coincident points, and the results which use causal perturbation theory for interacting fields can pin these sources instead of citing them from memory. Checked on 2026-11-02: Epstein and Glaser, bibliographic data (title, journal, volume 19 no. 3, pages 211-295, 1973) against the Numdam record; Brunetti and Fredenhagen, the arXiv abstract (a purely local version of the Stueckelberg-Bogoliubov-Epstein-Glaser method, extension of distributions) and the statements and numbering of Thms. 5.2 and 5.3 against the arXiv text; that text states the ambiguity of Thm. 5.3 through the values on chosen test functions, the form as a sum of derivatives of delta up to order sd - n appearing in the proof and its discussion; Scharf, title, edition, year and publisher against the Springer record and the chapter and section titles (3.1 to 3.13, 4.6 Gauge invariance and Ward identities, 5.3 Axial anomalies) against a library table of contents (the edition of that record not confirmed); Grigore, the arXiv abstract and introduction, which credits the earlier all-orders treatment of gauge invariance in QED and says its proof relies on reduction formulae for one-particle reducible graphs whose rigorous proof seems absent, and gives a reformulated proof; Duetsch and Fredenhagen, the arXiv abstract (interacting fields as formal power series in the local algebras without the adiabatic limit, the BRST transformation as a graded derivation implemented by a local Kugo-Ojima operator, stability of the Hilbert space structure, all assumptions verified in QED) and DOI; Hollands, the arXiv abstract (renormalised perturbative Yang-Mills on any globally hyperbolic background, Ward identities at the renormalised level keeping the interacting BRST current conserved and the BRST charge nilpotent, observables as the BRST cohomology) and DOI. Not checked against the sources: the journal page ranges of Brunetti-Fredenhagen, Duetsch-Fredenhagen and Hollands (from memory), the content of Epstein and Glaser beyond the title, the theorem-level statements of Scharf sec. 4.6, and the section numbers of Duetsch-Fredenhagen and Hollands cited by the causal spin-statistics result.

levels.formal:
Signature $(+,-,-,-)$, units $\hbar = c = 1$; free fields on flat spacetime, Wick polynomials of them, and a local interaction density $\mathcal{L}$ smeared with a test function $g$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Causal perturbation theory.)} The time-ordered products $T_{n}$ of Wick polynomials are constructed by induction on $n$ from causal factorisation ($T_{n}$ factorises into lower products when the points are causally ordered); at each order $T_{n}$ is fixed by the lower orders away from the total diagonal, and the only freedom is its extension across the diagonal, which can be chosen Poincar\'e covariant; the S-matrix and the interacting fields (Bogoliubov's formula) are formal power series in $g$ built from the $T_{n}$, with no ultraviolet regulator \cite{EpsteinGlaser1973}.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Extension by scaling degree.)} Let $t_{0}$ be a distribution on $\R^{n}\setminus\{0\}$ of scaling degree $\mathrm{sd}$ at the origin. If $\mathrm{sd} < n$ there is a unique extension $t$ to $\R^{n}$ with the same scaling degree. If $n \le \mathrm{sd} < \infty$, extensions with the same scaling degree exist, and two of them differ by $\sum_{|a| \le \omega}c_{a}\partial^{a}\delta$, $\omega = \mathrm{sd} - n$ \cite{BrunettiFredenhagen2000}. The same holds locally on any globally hyperbolic gravitational field, the scaling degree being read in local coordinates.
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Ward-preserving time-ordered products in electrodynamics.)} In quantum electrodynamics with the covariant (Gupta-Bleuler) photon the extensions of (i) can be normalised at every order so that perturbative gauge invariance holds; it implies the Ward identities, in particular the Ward-Takahashi identity of the vertex and the self-energy and the transversality of the vacuum polarisation \cite{Scharf1995, Grigore1999}.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Local construction and BRST structure in electrodynamics.)} The interacting fields of (i) generate local algebras without the adiabatic limit; for electrodynamics the BRST transformation is a graded derivation of the interacting field algebra, implemented by a local Kugo-Ojima operator, and the positive Hilbert space structure of the physical states of the free theory is stable under the perturbation \cite{DutschFredenhagen1999}.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Yang-Mills.)} Perturbative Yang-Mills theory with ghosts and antifields is renormalisable on every globally hyperbolic gravitational field, flat spacetime included, with Ward identities at the renormalised level that keep the interacting BRST current conserved and the interacting BRST charge nilpotent; the physical observables are the BRST cohomology \cite{Hollands2008}.
\end{enumerate}
levels.technical: Causal perturbation theory, due to Epstein and Glaser, builds the time-ordered products of an interacting quantum field theory order by order from causality alone. At each order the product is already determined away from the points where all arguments coincide; the ultraviolet problem is only how to extend a distribution across that set, and no regulator is introduced. Brunetti and Fredenhagen put the extension step in a local form ordered by the scaling degree: a distribution of scaling degree below the dimension has one extension of the same degree, and at or above the dimension extensions exist and differ by finitely many derivatives of the delta function, the local counterterms. For electrodynamics Scharf showed in this framework that the free normalisation can be chosen so that gauge invariance, and with it the Ward identities, hold at every order (a later proof by Grigore repairs a step that rests on reduction formulae). Duetsch and Fredenhagen constructed the local algebras of interacting fields and implemented the BRST symmetry of electrodynamics by a local Kugo-Ojima operator, with the positivity of the physical states preserved. Hollands extended the construction to Yang-Mills theory on any globally hyperbolic gravitational field, with Ward identities that keep the interacting BRST charge nilpotent.
levels.lay: The infinities of quantum field theory can be avoided without any artificial cut-off. Epstein and Glaser showed that the calculation can be built up step by step from the requirement that cause precedes effect; the only freedom left at each step is how to treat the points where particles meet, and that freedom is a short list of constants. Later work showed that this freedom can be used to keep the conservation of electric charge exact at every step, constructed the local quantities of the theory directly, and extended the construction to the force fields of the strong and weak interactions, on flat spacetime and in gravitational fields. The series takes these results from the literature.
levels.one-liner: Causal perturbation theory (Epstein-Glaser): time-ordered products fixed off the diagonal, extension by scaling degree unique below the dimension and ambiguous by derivatives of delta up to order sd minus the dimension above it (Brunetti-Fredenhagen Thms. 5.2, 5.3); Ward-preserving normalisation in electrodynamics (Scharf; Grigore); local interacting fields and BRST for QED (Duetsch-Fredenhagen 1999); renormalised Yang-Mills with a nilpotent interacting BRST charge (Hollands 2008).
